# watchpoint_external_vault_federation (Data Source)

The federated identity Watchpoint presents to a vault vendor, so the trust policy on the vendor side can be built from the same values Watchpoint will actually send.

```terraform
data "watchpoint_external_vault_federation" "aws" {
  kind = "aws-secrets-manager"
}

resource "aws_iam_openid_connect_provider" "watchpoint" {
  url             = data.watchpoint_external_vault_federation.aws.issuer
  client_id_list  = [data.watchpoint_external_vault_federation.aws.audience]
}
```

Pin `subject` in the trust policy. Without it, any Watchpoint tenant could authenticate against it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "watchpoint_external_vault_federation" "gcp" {
  kind = "gcp-secret-manager"
}

# Federation cannot work until the issuer is a public HTTPS address, because your
# cloud fetches the discovery document itself. Fail here rather than in Google's
# error message.
resource "google_iam_workload_identity_pool_provider" "watchpoint" {
  workload_identity_pool_id          = google_iam_workload_identity_pool.watchpoint.workload_identity_pool_id
  workload_identity_pool_provider_id = "watchpoint"

  oidc {
    issuer_uri = data.watchpoint_external_vault_federation.gcp.issuer
  }

  attribute_mapping = { "google.subject" = "assertion.sub" }

  # Without this, any Watchpoint tenant could exchange a token against this pool.
  attribute_condition = "assertion.sub == '${data.watchpoint_external_vault_federation.gcp.subject}'"

  lifecycle {
    precondition {
      condition     = data.watchpoint_external_vault_federation.gcp.reachable
      error_message = "The Watchpoint issuer is not a public HTTPS address yet, so Google cannot fetch its discovery document."
    }
  }
}

# Google's audience is the pool provider path you just created, which is why it
# is a config field rather than a constant Watchpoint hands over. The data source
# says so through audience_from_field.
resource "watchpoint_external_vault" "gcp" {
  slug         = "prod-gcp"
  name         = "Production Google Secret Manager"
  kind         = "gcp-secret-manager"
  token_source = "federated"

  config = {
    project_id      = "my-project"
    audience        = "//iam.googleapis.com/${google_iam_workload_identity_pool_provider.watchpoint.name}"
    service_account = google_service_account.watchpoint_reader.email
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `kind` (String) Vendor to report the audience for, for example `aws-secrets-manager`. `issuer`, `discovery_url`, `jwks_url` and `subject` are the same for every vendor; only the audience differs.

### Read-Only

- `audience` (String) The audience for this vendor. Empty when the vendor's audience is a value you create rather than one Watchpoint hands over (Google's workload identity pool path, for example); `audience_from_field` then names the `config` key to put it in.
- `audience_from_field` (String) When `audience` is empty, the `watchpoint_external_vault.config` key that the audience you create belongs in. Empty otherwise.
- `discovery_url` (String) The OIDC discovery document. Your cloud fetches this itself, so it has to be reachable from the vendor's network, not just from you.
- `issuer` (String) The `iss` of every assertion Watchpoint mints, and the OIDC issuer to register with the vendor.
- `jwks_url` (String) The signing keys. Vendors that do not do full OIDC discovery (HashiCorp Vault's JWKS mode, Conjur, Akeyless) want this directly.
- `reachable` (Boolean) False when the issuer is not a public HTTPS address, which means the vendor cannot fetch the discovery document and federation cannot work yet. Worth asserting on with a `precondition` rather than discovering it from the vendor's error message.
- `signing_algorithm` (String) Signature algorithm of the assertion, for vendors that ask.
- `subject` (String) The `sub` Watchpoint asserts for THIS tenant. Pin the trust policy to it exactly; a wildcard would let any Watchpoint tenant authenticate against your vault.
- `supported` (Boolean) False for vendors with no federation option at all (Delinea Secret Server, BeyondTrust Password Safe, the CyberArk Central Credential Provider). Those need `token_source = "client_credentials"`, `"mtls"` or `"local"` instead.
